page: Microsoft Azure E4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance is powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor utilizing the x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core at a clock speed of 4.2 GHz. The CPU features 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 260 MB of L3 cache, alongside hardware instruction support for AVX-512, AMX, AES, and SHA-NI. The instance is allocated 32.0 GB of system memory, providing an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio. It does not include bundled local storage or integrated GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate mid-range single-threaded processing and lower multi-threaded throughput due to the 4-vCPU count. In PassMark, the CPU achieved an overall score of 7386.87, extended instructions reached 5628.14, and database operations scored 2843.43. Geekbench evaluations recorded a single-core score of 1664.0 alongside a multi-core score of 3798.0. Single-threaded gzip compression scored strongly at 31.25 GB/sec, whereas uncached large block memory bandwidth registered at 36.52 GB/sec read and 25.66 GB/sec write. Multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and Redis SET operations placed in the lower quartile, reflecting constrained scaling across its 4 virtual cores.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E4s_v6 offers a high memory-to-core ratio suited for applications where RAM capacity requirements exceed raw computational parallelism. The absence of local disk resources necessitates external storage volumes for stateful persistence. The configuration is aligned with in-memory caching tiers, small-to-medium relational database instances, text processing, and static web serving workloads requiring elevated RAM density without substantial multi-threaded compute demands.
description: Microsoft Azure E4s_v6 is a memory-optimized virtual machine designed for workloads that prioritize memory capacity over high multi-threaded compute throughput. Operating on Microsoft Hyper-V, the system provides 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at 4.2 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, supported by 260 MB of L3 cache and advanced instruction sets including AVX-512 and AMX. The instance includes 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding an 8.0 GB per vCPU ratio, with no bundled local storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmarks demonstrate solid single-thread performance, highlighted by strong single-threaded gzip compression of 31.25 GB/sec and an average PassMark CPU score of 7386.87, though multi-core metrics and memory bandwidth test in the lower quartiles. The hardware balance provides resource efficiency for memory-heavy operations, making the server suitable for relational databases, in-memory caching, static web serving, and lightweight enterprise applications.
